content:
# Analysis

Looking at the error and comparing `dev/app.yaml` with `prod/app.yaml`:

**dev/app.yaml Deployment** (known-good):
```yaml
selector:
  matchLabels:
    app: myapp
    env: dev
template:
  metadata:
    labels:
      app: myapp
      env: dev
```

**prod/app.yaml Deployment** (defect):
```yaml
selector:
  matchLabels:
    app: myapp
    env: prod
    version: v2          # ← Required by selector
template:
  metadata:
    labels:
      app: myapp
      env: prod          # ← Missing "version: v2"
```

## Identified Issue

The selector requires the label **`version: v2`**, but the pod template provides only `app` and `env` labels. 

## Fix

Add `version: v2` to `spec.template.metadata.labels` in the Deployment. This will:
1. Satisfy the Deployment's selector (all selector labels will be present on pods)
2. Keep the Service selector working (it only requires `app` and `env`, which remain present)

---

`prod/app.yaml`
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ServiceAccount
metadata:
  name: myapp-prod
  namespace: app
  annotations:
    eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn: "<REPLACE_WITH_myapp-prod-service-role_ARN_AFTER_CREATE>"
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: myapp-prod
  namespace: app
  labels:
    app: myapp
    env: prod
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: myapp
      env: prod
      version: v2
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: myapp
        env: prod
        version: v2
    spec:
      serviceAccountName: myapp-prod
      containers:
        - name: myapp
          image: docker.io/myapp/myapp:latest
          ports:
            - containerPort: 8080
          resources:
            requests:
              cpu: 100m
              memory: 128Mi
            limits:
              cpu: 500m
              memory: 256Mi
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: myapp-prod
  namespace: app
spec:
  selector:
    app: myapp
    env: prod
  ports:
    - port: 80
      targetPort: 8080
  type: ClusterIP
```
